summary: codes missing ['default']; codes extra ['4XX', '5XX']; 1 absent, 3 differing, 2 extra

answer.why_different: The generated document simplifies the response descriptions and changes the response structure: the detailed default error response is replaced by explicit 4XX and 5XX ranges. The likely cause is value-level prose loss combined with a structural change from a catch-all response to response-code ranges.
answer.spec_3gpp: The specification requires 200, 201 and 204 behavior with distinct conditions, and specifies ErrorResponse for 4xx/5xx errors. It does not require a particular OpenAPI default-versus-range representation, but the success-response conditions and response-body behavior are normative or otherwise specified.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI permits a default response for undeclared status codes and permits uppercase 4XX and 5XX response ranges. Response descriptions should document the expected response, and the Responses Object must contain at least one response.
answer.clearer_why: The official descriptions explain when each success status is returned and whether a representation is present. The generated descriptions are shorter but omit important conditions, including the 200 replacement/update distinction and the 204 requirement that the representations be identical.

citations.quote: Resource 200 OK ... Status code returned when the resource is replaced, and when the replaced resource representation is not identical to the resource representation in the request.
ErrorResponse | 4xx/5xx | Returned in case of an error
To define a range of response codes, this field MAY contain the uppercase wildcard character `X`.

4XX:
      description: Error response for a 4XX client error

differences.reason: The generated description loses the specified conditions for returning 200 and omits that the updated resource representation is returned in the response body. The specification explicitly distinguishes replacement, non-identical updates, identical updates, and the returned representation (S3).

The generated description says only “Created” and omits that 201 is returned when the resource is created and that the created representation is returned in the response body. This information is present in the official response (C1) and is consistent with the specified PUT response behavior (S3).

The generated description omits the restriction that 204 may be returned only when the replaced representation is identical to the request and omits the no-body statement. The official response carries both constraints (C1).

The generated side removes the official catch-all error response and its ErrorResponseDefault schema. Although OpenAPI allows explicit ranges, removing the default loses the official documentation of responses other than the specifically declared codes (O1, O4; C1).

An explicit 4XX response range is valid OpenAPI and directly represents the specification’s documented 4xx error response with ErrorResponse (S4, O5). It is more specific than the official catch-all for client errors.

An explicit 5XX response range is valid OpenAPI and directly represents the specification’s documented 5xx error response with ErrorResponse (S4, O5). It is more specific than the official catch-all for server errors.

#### Responses Object  
A container for the expected responses of an operation.
The container maps a HTTP response code to the expected response.  
The documentation is not necessarily expected to cover all possible HTTP response codes because they may not be known in advance.
However, documentation is expected to cover a successful operation response and any known errors.  
The `default` MAY be used as a default response object for all HTTP codes
that are not covered individually by the specification.  
The `Responses Object` MUST contain at least one response code, and it
SHOULD be the response for a successful operation call.  
##### Fixed Fields
Field Name | Type | Description
---|:---:|---

---|:---:|--- [HTTP Status Code](#http-status-codes) | [Response Object](#response-object) \| [Reference Object](#reference-object) | Any [HTTP status code](#http-status-codes) can be used as the property name, but only one property per code, to describe the expected response for that HTTP status code. A [Reference Object](#reference-object) can link to a response that is defined in the [OpenAPI Object's components/responses](#componentsResponses) section. This field MUST be enclosed in quotation marks (for example, "200") for compatibility between JSON and YAML. To define a range of response codes, this field MAY contain the uppercase wildcard character `X`. For example, `2XX` represents all response codes between `[200-299]`. The following range definitions are allowed: `1XX`, `2XX`, `3XX`, `4XX`, and `5XX`. If a response range is defined using an explicit code, the explicit code definition takes precedence over the range definition for that code.
